title: Boundary symmetry and approximation repeatedly fail without interior positivity
claim: Two failed analytic routes expose the same missing implication: a representation can approximate zeta or have the correct unit-modulus boundary symmetry while still lacking the interior zero-free, Hardy-norm, or positivity control needed to force critical-line zeros.
historical_or_program_relation: The counterexamples collected in the 2004 overview and the later local-factor obstruction in the semi-local operator program both turn an attractive representation into a diagnostic: the decisive burden is the stronger interior sign or norm property, not the already-visible boundary behavior.
limits: The Dirichlet-partial-sum, de Branges-space, and Hardy-space settings are mathematically distinct, so this relation does not identify one common positivity theorem or rule out repaired versions of any program.

title: Gram-point sign tests became local detectors inside a two-certificate proof
claim: Phase normalization makes critical-line zeros detectable by real sign changes, but Gram-interval occupancy is not reliable enough to certify completeness; only agreement between an on-line witness count and an independent global zero count excludes off-line zeros in a bounded region.
historical_or_program_relation: The historical Gram-law failures forced computation away from one-root-per-cell reasoning toward neighborhood repair and then toward certificate composition: Hardy-Z sign changes supply located witnesses while the argument principle or Backlund count supplies the exhaustive cardinality.
limits: The agreement certifies only the bounded contour whose numerical errors and total count are controlled; it neither proves RH above the cutoff nor makes every individual Gram interval trustworthy.

title: A finite zero census becomes global evidence only through a separate analytic transfer
claim: Even an exhaustive finite prefix of critical-line zeros implies only a bounded-height RH statement by itself; the 2021 computation obtains an unconditional global statement about the de Bruijn-Newman constant only because a previously proved threshold theorem converts verified height into an upper bound for Lambda.
historical_or_program_relation: The relation marks a change in what large computations can license: Lehmer's census ends at its height, whereas the later verification is composed with heat-flow analysis to cross from finite certification to a global but weaker parameter bound.
limits: The transfer yields only the stated Lambda bound and does not prove RH; no amount of verified height may be described as global without the hypotheses and constants of an applicable transfer theorem.

title: The finite-field avatar isolates positivity as the missing transferable operation
claim: The finite-field model succeeds not merely because it has correspondences, but because geometry forces a negative or positive-definite form; constructing higher-genus correspondences or semi-local trace operators without the analogous norm, index, and globally compatible normalization leaves the zero-location mechanism incomplete.
historical_or_program_relation: The historical avatar first identifies intersection-form sign as a working mechanism, the higher-genus reconstruction records that the carrier algebra does not automatically bring its norm, and the semi-local analytic route relocates the same obstruction to compatible principal-value normalizations in an explicit-formula trace.
limits: Divisor intersections, correspondence norms, and semi-local principal values are not identified as the same object, and the sources provide no transfer theorem from finite-field geometry to the classical zeta function.

title: Spectral counting agreement remains strictly below a Hilbert-Polya correspondence
claim: Matching the high-energy zeta zero count or the symplectic area of a cutoff region can preserve the leading spectral density while forgetting phase, boundary sign, and the exhaustive correspondence between every nontrivial zero and a self-adjoint spectrum that Hilbert-Polya requires.
historical_or_program_relation: Later prolate and scaling-Hamiltonian constructions realize increasingly concrete pieces of the spectral analogy, but Conrey's audit fixes the unchanged proof burden: a noncircular natural operator must account for all zeros, not merely reproduce their Weyl-scale count.
limits: Asymptotic count matching can still be structurally informative and is not evidence against the models; the relation only denies that such matching by itself proves self-adjoint spectral realization or RH.

title: Ordering, branch, and principal-value conventions carry arithmetic information
claim: In prime-zero and phase formulas, the limiting prescription is mathematical data: changing the zero ordering, choosing a principal phase, or mismatching local principal values can alter a conditional sum, inject and cancel a zero-counting staircase, or spoil the intended global trace.
historical_or_program_relation: Riemann's contour-height ordering already prevents free rearrangement of the zero sum; later phase criteria reveal hidden branch corrections involving N(T), while the semi-local program identifies compatible global normalization as the obstruction to assembling canonical local traces.
limits: These are three different normalization problems, not proof that their corrections coincide or that the associated explicit formulas are invalid when their prescribed conventions are followed.

title: Equivalent criteria preserve truth while relocating, not removing, the proof burden
claim: Farey discrepancy, cyclotomic growth, function-space density, coefficient positivity, determinants, and divisor inequalities can each encode RH exactly while exposing incompatible observables; equivalence alone supplies no mechanism connecting those observables or reason that one representation is easier to control.
historical_or_program_relation: The expanding historical catalogue of RH equivalents broadens the available interfaces, but the later comparisons make the obstruction explicit: every translation moves the hard estimate into a new norm, infinite sign family, finite determinant growth, or arithmetic inequality.
limits: The relation does not weaken the logical equivalences or preclude a criterion from becoming fruitful; it specifically rejects treating shared equivalence to RH as a demonstrated cross-method mechanism.

title: The Tauberian bridge explains why PNT needs less zero control than RH
claim: For prime asymptotics, logarithmic differentiation and Tauberian transfer need nonvanishing only on Re(s)=1, whereas the explicit formula makes the stronger RH error scale depend on forcing every zero real part from the boundary value 1 down to 1/2.
historical_or_program_relation: The successful prime-number-theorem route isolates a minimal analytic boundary condition and a theorem that returns to counting; later explicit-formula accounts show precisely why that historical success does not close the sharper zero-location burden posed by RH.
limits: This relation proves no new zero-free region and does not say that Tauberian methods cannot contribute to RH; it distinguishes the zero control sufficient for the two stated conclusions.

title: Newman lower bounds progressed from exceptional witnesses to collective gap rigidity
claim: Finite Jensen or Lehmer-pair certificates establish lower bounds on Lambda through exceptional local obstructions, but the proof that Lambda is nonnegative uses a different quantifier: any negative-time real-zero phase would force almost all normalized gaps toward a lattice, contradicting a positive proportion of small zeta gaps.
historical_or_program_relation: The program moves from computationally finding one obstruction at a chosen deformation time, through pair-specific heat-flow bounds, to a dynamical-energy argument that rules out the entire negative-time regime by aggregate gap behavior.
limits: A failed finite witness search proves nothing, and no collection of the cited finite certificates alone yields Lambda>=0; the collective argument additionally depends on its heat-flow analysis and the external small-gap theorem.

title: A close zero pair became relevant only after its global environment was certified
claim: Near-cancellation and an unusually small raw gap motivate targeted computation, but a pair affects the de Bruijn-Newman boundary only after scaling to the heat-family coordinates and bounding its interaction with the full zero configuration through g_k with one-sided numerical control.
historical_or_program_relation: Lehmer's 1956 close-zero phenomenon supplied a search heuristic; the 1993 work turned such a discovered pair into a compositional certificate whose local high-precision window, remote-zero bounds, and upward-rounded sum establish the Lehmer criterion and hence a Lambda lower bound.
limits: The recurrence heuristic neither predicts an RH counterexample nor proves search optimality, and a certified pair supplies only its stated lower bound rather than exhaustive information about all zeros or the exact value of Lambda.

title: Random-matrix evidence sharpened from spacing resemblance to a family-indexed probability law
claim: The transferable random-matrix object is not an arbitrary deterministic unitary polynomial but a symmetry class and probability law selected by an arithmetic L-function family; rare deterministic counterexamples can coexist with statistical predictions, while any deeper model must still reproduce irregular gaps and exceptional multiplicities rather than smoothing them away.
historical_or_program_relation: Early spacing correlations suggested a missing spectral or cohomological structure, Katz-Sarnak supplied the family-to-compact-group mechanism in the finite-field model, and later analogy audits separated model-typical predictions from properties of every matrix while retaining Conrey's adequacy test for exceptional arithmetic behavior.
limits: The finite-field family theorem does not establish the classical zeta correspondence, model-conditional rarity is not an arithmetic proof, and none of these units constructs a Hilbert-Polya operator or proves RH.

title: Physical and spectral representations must audit where the target structure entered
claim: A representation can appear to generate the desired zeta symmetry or zero data while actually importing it through a critical-line parametrization, a boundary-conditioned initial state, or a branch correction containing N(T); tracing those inputs is necessary to distinguish explanation from repackaging.
historical_or_program_relation: The Hilbert-Polya audit states the noncircular correspondence requirement, the unfolded particle-in-a-box example locates the supposedly absent conjugate branch in the initial condition, and the phase criterion reveals the zero-counting staircase hidden inside principal-argument bookkeeping.
limits: Hidden structure is not automatically illegitimate if independently derived, and these examples do not rule out physical models; they identify distinct places where a claimed bridge must prove rather than assume its zeta-specific content.

title: An isolated tiny gap is decisive for one interface and insufficient for another
claim: A tiny adjacent-zero gap can be a sufficient local witness for a de Bruijn-Newman lower bound once normalized by the entire zero environment, yet isolated tiny or large gaps cannot supply the positive measure required to explain the bulk Gaussian distribution of log|Z|.
historical_or_program_relation: The two programs assign the same conspicuous local event different evidentiary roles: heat-flow theory converts one certified configuration into a phase-boundary inequality, whereas the value-distribution audit tests and rejects isolated-gap dominance by comparing its available measure with Selberg-scale bulk mass.
limits: The heat-flow statement is a theorem conditional on its pair certificate, while the bulk-carrier rejection is a heuristic inconsistency argument; neither says that local gaps make no contribution outside the specific target being tested.

title: Global zero counting was repurposed from completeness certificate to local detector control
claim: An aggregate zero-count theorem can close information missing from a local observable in two concrete ways: it can match critical-line sign-change witnesses to certify a bounded census, or it can bound the remote-zero tail in a mollified zero-free-region detector.
historical_or_program_relation: The argument-principle count first serves as the exhaustive half of finite RH verification; in the later detector architecture, a uniform N(T) remainder becomes a reusable tail-error input that lets local integral and positivity estimates be separated from distant zeros.
limits: Tail control does not locate individual zeros or prove the zero-free region by itself, and bounded census matching requires its own controlled contour evaluation; the two uses share an aggregate-count interface, not an identical proof.

title: Completion reduced RH to real-rootedness but left sign production as the historical burden
claim: Jacobi inversion, completion, and recentering make xi entire, even, and real on the relevant axis, converting critical-line location into a real-rootedness problem; those symmetries do not produce real zeros, so later work must add a sign-change or moment-rigidity mechanism.
historical_or_program_relation: Riemann's cosine-kernel representation makes reflection and decay visible, the modern canonical formulation states the exact real-rootedness reduction, and the 1953 Fourier-moment route shows the additional tail-sign-to-derivative chain needed even to force infinitely many critical-line zeros.
limits: The cited moment unit stops before its intended final contradiction, and infinitely many on-line zeros would still be weaker than all zeros on the line; evenness and reality alone imply neither conclusion.

title: Heat flow is useful because it orders root geometry, unlike generic value perturbation
claim: Zero alignment is unstable under changing the target value of a meromorphic function, but the de Bruijn-Newman heat deformation has a monotone real-rootedness property that compresses all times into a single phase boundary; the latter structure, not perturbation alone, makes cross-time inference possible.
historical_or_program_relation: Value-distribution theory warns that the zero fiber is exceptional among nearby a-point fibers, while the heat-family program succeeds in organizing a different deformation by an order parameter Lambda whose value at time zero is equivalent to the RH question.
limits: Changing the value a and evolving by the heat equation are different perturbations, so their stability properties are not contradictory; monotonicity defines a useful framework but does not determine Lambda or prove RH.
